record.paper_title: Optimal Algorithms for Numerical Integration: Recent Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: For randomized numerical integration on the classical smoothness classes F_d^k = {f:[0,1]^d -> R : ||D^alpha f||_infty <= 1 for every multi-index alpha with |alpha| <= k}, upper bounds of the form d^t n^(-k/d-1/2) are known. What is the smallest possible exponent t in the dimension factor d^t for such randomized upper bounds?

evidence.quote: Open Problem: Study, similarly as in Theorem 1, the dependence on the dimension for randomized algorithms. Using results of Krieg [53] one can prove upper bounds of the form dt n-k/d-1/2. One may take t = (k+1)/2, but the optimal (smallest) t is not known.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For integers $d,k\geq 1$, let
\[
F_d^k \;=\; \{\, f:[0,1]^d\to\mathbb{R} \;:\; \|D^\alpha f\|_\infty \le 1 \text{ for every multi-index } \alpha \text{ with } |\alpha|\le k \,\}.
\]
A randomized cubature algorithm $A_n$ using at most $n$ function values is a (measurable) mapping that, given a random seed $\omega$, produces an approximation $A_n(f,\omega)$ to the integral $I(f)=\int_{[0,1]^d} f(x)\,dx$. Its worst-case randomized error on $F_d^k$ is
\[
e^{\mathrm{ran}}(n,F_d^k) \;=\; \inf_{A_n}\; \sup_{f\in F_d^k}\; \bigl(\mathbb{E}\,|I(f)-A_n(f,\cdot)|^2\bigr)^{1/2}.
\]
It is known that for some constants $C(k)$ independent of $d$ and $n$, there exist randomized algorithms achieving an upper bound of the form
\[
e^{\mathrm{ran}}(n,F_d^k) \;\le\; C(k)\, d^{\,t}\, n^{-k/d-1/2},
\]
and one may take $t=(k+1)/2$.

Determine the smallest exponent $t=t(k)\ge 0$ for which an upper bound of the above form
\[
e^{\mathrm{ran}}(n,F_d^k) \;\le\; C(k)\, d^{\,t}\, n^{-k/d-1/2}
\]
holds for all $d,n\ge 1$ with some constant $C(k)$ depending only on $k$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in a recent survey on optimal algorithms for numerical integration. The available upper bound uses t=(k+1)/2, derived from results of Krieg, but the optimal (smallest) exponent t is stated to be unknown. Recent works on high-dimensional integration (e.g., Goda–Krieg 2024) achieve dimension-independent rates in weighted Korobov classes, but do not pin down the optimal t for the classical class F_d^k. No publication found that settles the optimal exponent.

status_evidence.title: Optimal Algorithms for Numerical Integration: Recent Results and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: One may take t = (k+1)/2, but the optimal (smallest) t is not known.
status_evidence.claim: The optimal exponent t in the randomized upper bound d^t n^{-k/d-1/2} on F_d^k is explicitly listed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: A simple universal algorithm for high-dimensional integration
status_evidence.snippet: A simple universal algorithm... has the optimal error rate (independent of the dimension) in all weighted Korobov classes both in the randomized and the deterministic setting.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work addresses dimension-independent randomized rates but in weighted Korobov classes, not resolving the optimal t for F_d^k.
